A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GMValuator and retain identifiable methodological and experimental content. All nine pages of v4 and thirteen pages of v5, including Appendices A–F, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the material.

before.justification: v4 reports original CIFAR-10 distribution visualizations and statistical comparisons, plus qualitative CelebA attribution results in Figures 2–4 and Table 1.

after.justification: v5 reports original class and attribute comparisons, noisy-data rankings, runtime measurements, and supplementary sensitivity experiments in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v5 retains PQ-based matching but adds perceptual re-ranking with LPIPS or DreamSim and MANIQA-based generated-image quality assessment. Its contribution function multiplies normalized similarity scores by image quality before aggregation, substantively changing valuation beyond v4's distance-based credits.

E1.justification: Beyond v4's MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CelebA scope, v5 evaluates high-resolution animal faces through AFHQ and human faces through FFHQ. It also introduces a Gaussian-corrupted MNIST data-cleansing scenario, expanding both represented domains and evaluation conditions.

E2.justification: v4 evaluates no external data-valuation baseline. v5 adds VAE-TracIn to the identical-class and runtime comparisons in Tables II and IV, and IF4GAN to noisy-data ranking and runtime comparisons in Figure 5 and Table IV.

E3.justification: v5 introduces quantitative class agreement using 100 generated samples and k=30, 50, 100, attribute agreement at k=5, 10, 15, corruption-ranking evaluation using 10,000 generated images, and timing protocols. It adds beta-VAE evaluations and changes the reported CelebA generator from StyleGAN2 to Diffusion-StyleGAN. The retained training/non-training experiment's Xv1/Xv2 swap is a relabeling.

E4.justification: v5 adds comparisons with and without re-ranking and across distance metrics, noisy-data ranking analysis, and generated-sample-size sensitivity testing in Appendix C. Figure 3 also examines the equal-credit problem using normal versus uniform latent sampling. These substantially extend v4's proximity tests and qualitative high/low-value face examples.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly specifies ten repetitions with resampled generated sets and adds variability plots; its prose describes mean and standard deviation, although Figure 7 displays boxplots. Appendix A revises the inherited test hypotheses and corrects the p-value wording while retaining the original test statistics. Repeated-run uncertainty remains limited to the supplementary sensitivity study.

E6.justification: v5 adds extensive class, attribute, cleansing, runtime, and sensitivity results. For example, Table II reports CIFAR-10 class agreement of 77.94% for DreamSim versus 6.28% for VAE-TracIn at k=30; Table IV reports noisy-MNIST valuation times of 17,086 seconds for DreamSim versus 14,543 for IF4GAN. These are new comparisons. The earlier statistical means, p-values, and t-statistics are retained after matching the swapped subset labels.

T1.justification: v5 removes the explicit Wasserstein/coupling formulation, specifies deduplicated training data, extends the contribution definition with quality weighting, and adds a brief O(mnC)-to-O(mQD) recall-complexity argument. These are limited formal revisions around the retained similarity-score aggregation; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v5 narrows v4's broad claim of being the first generative-model data-valuation work to being the first model-agnostic, training-free approach, acknowledging existing model-specific methods. It also elevates image-quality calibration and four evaluation criteria into explicit contributions in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive explanations of equal-credit bias for poor generated images, accumulated contributions from distant samples, and the accuracy/runtime tradeoff of DreamSim. It attributes VAE-TracIn's weak CIFAR-10 results to possible underfitting and identifies other modalities as future validation. v4 mainly interprets training-set proximity and qualitative facial resemblance; its applications discussion survives in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v5 newly provides hardware specifications in Table I, expanded dataset and model information in Appendix E, and layer/latent specifications in Table VII, substantially extending v4's sparse implementation documentation. Reliability is limited by reversed CPU/GPU labels and apparently swapped BigGAN/beta-VAE headings. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v5 substantially revises positioning by acknowledging and discussing IF4GAN and VAE-TracIn, distinguishing concurrent LAVA, and organizing valuation methods into metric-based, influence-based, and data-driven approaches. New references supporting DreamSim, MANIQA, and evaluation criteria further expand the discussion beyond v4's largely discriminative-model literature.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, formulation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. v5 organizes the method around explicit challenges and modules, replaces the research-assumption experiment structure with four criteria, and moves retained statistical and applications material into Appendices A and F. The title and author line also change.

P2.justification: v5 redraws the pipeline and distribution visualization, replaces the earlier high/low-value face displays with contributor grids, and adds quality examples, a violin plot, sensitivity boxplots, and structured experimental tables. The original statistical table is relocated to Appendix A, while typography, captions, and table organization are substantially revised.

improvement.justification: v4's validation relied mainly on proximity assumptions, one statistical comparison, and qualitative face matches, without evaluated valuation baselines. v5 substantially addresses that weakness through baseline comparisons, quantitative attribution tests, cleansing and runtime evaluation, and repeated-sample sensitivity analysis, while narrowing its novelty claim. Contradictory wording in Table V, mislabeled technical tables, and inconsistent sample-size labels limit reliability, but the stronger comparative evidence and more accurate positioning provide a substantial net improvement.
